entries.title: II Samuel 9:1
segments: True piety will be grateful, not only to God the author of all good, but to those who imitate him, and through whom his goodness is displayed; and it will manifest itself not only towards them, but when practicable towards others who are connected with them.

entries.title: II Samuel 9:3
segments: The kindness of God; kindness exercised in the fear of God, in accordance with his oath to Jonathan.

entries.title: II Samuel 9:4
segments: Lo-debar; east of Jordan, in the land of Gilead.

entries.title: II Samuel 9:7
segments:
Thy father; his grandfather. 
 
The good character and conduct of parents, and their kindness, especially to the distressed, are often followed by great blessings on their children.

entries.title: II Samuel 9:8
segments:
A dead dog; an expression of great unworthiness of such distinguished favors. 
 
A conviction of unworthiness, and true gratitude for favors, tend greatly to increase the liberality and usefulness of the giver, and also the happiness and benefit of the receiver.

entries.title: II Samuel 9:10
segments: May have food to eat; though Mephibosheth himself sat at the king's table, he needed a suitable provision for his household.

entries.title: II Samuel 9:13
segments: Bodily infirmities, though a present calamity to thise who suffer them, may be overruled for their highest good.
